bullets: The model picker now shows thinking-level options when a catalog lists only one model with a reasoning ladder.
The message shown when you run out of time on a paid model now tells you exactly how many hours that model consumes and how many hours you have left.
When Freebuff blocks a message because you lack enough time for the chosen model, the assistant now opens the model selection menu instead of showing an error.
The assistant now asks you questions much less often, saving the interactive question tool for rare cases where progress is completely blocked.
When an advertiser funds a coding task, the assistant now uses a safer, more automated tool to install software packages.
The instructions for sponsored tasks now explain that pinned package lists set exact versions, but do not stop the AI from adding other packages it needs.
The Freebuff model picker can now hide all options except one fast, low-cost model called DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, based on a new switch in the General settings.
The Freebuff command line tool now saves your input history to disk using a two-step process that protects your history from corruption if storage runs out.
The system now requires the assistant to produce a short, cleaned-up closing note for advertisers that strips out personal details, code, and secrets before sharing it.
The instructions given to the AI for sponsored tasks are now trimmed to remove unnecessary background details, reducing the memory used per task.
Advertisers buying sponsored tasks can now add up to three extra checks that confirm specific code changes landed in a project.
